name: Charging & Starting
description: Alternator, starter motor, the long main positive cable from the trunk battery to the engine bay, the front power junction (remote jump post), alternator charge wire and ECM-controlled alternator interface, starter trigger and the clamps/grommets/heat protection along the way.

components.name: Alternator
components.description: Belt-driven alternator on the Gen V LT front accessory drive. The OE unit is ECM-controlled (GM 'L' terminal turn-on and 'F' field-duty feedback) so a standalone ECU must either drive the L terminal or the alternator must be converted to self-regulating. 170 A class OE units are common on LT1/LT4. A road-race car can downsize if the load budget allows (fans, fuel pumps and cool-suit are the big loads).
components.location: Front of engine, on the accessory drive bracket (driver side upper front on the Camaro LT1/LT4 installation – confirm on your engine).

factory.name: GM 170 A alternator (2016–2020 Camaro 6.2 L, aftermarket interchange listings)
factory.notes: Part number from aftermarket interchange listings, not a GM catalog page; confirm with a GM dealer VIN lookup.

raceOptions.name: Lightweight race alternator (self-exciting, 1-wire or 3-wire) on custom bracket
raceOptions.notes: Removes dependency on ECM L-terminal control; choose amperage ≥ calculated running load + 20 %.

raceOptions.name: Retain OE alternator, controlled by race ECU or PDM
raceOptions.notes: MoTeC/PDM can drive the L terminal (12 V switched via resistor) – keep the OE unit for reliability.

hardware.notes: GM LS/LT alternator mounting bolts are commonly specified at 50 N·m; confirm in GM SI for the LT1/LT4.
Typical GM alternator battery-terminal nut torque – hold the stud's insulated boot; do not over-torque (cracks the insulator).

installNotes: Install with the engine accessory drive (phase 6–7), wire it in phase 8.
Before startup, confirm the L-terminal is driven (or the unit is self-exciting); otherwise it will not charge.
Check belt alignment with a straightedge; wrap angle matters at sustained 7000 rpm.
inspection: B+ nut tight, boot in place.

images.title: GM 84143540 170 A alternator (2015-2020 Camaro/Tahoe) – eBay listing

modelRef.dimensions: Body Ø~145 mm, ~165 mm long + 26 mm 6-rib pulley (Ø~57 mm); pulley face in the accessory-belt plane (x ≈ -0.35).
modelRef.features: Cast aluminium front/rear housings with vent windows, steel stator band, black plastic rear cover, B+ stud with red boot, 2-pin L/F regulator socket, 3 bolt bosses.

components.name: Alternator control connector (L / F terminals)
components.description: 2-pin control connector on the OE regulator: L terminal (turn-on/regulation command from the ECM) and F terminal (field duty-cycle feedback to the ECM). With the Chevrolet Performance controller kit this is part of the engine harness; with a race ECU, wire L to a PWM/switched output and F to a digital/frequency input for logging.

hardware.spec: OE 2-way sealed connector with CPA lock

installNotes: Secure the lead to the alternator bracket with a P-clamp so it can't chafe on the belt.

modelRef.dimensions: 2-way sealed GM connector ~30 x 22 x 20 mm (estimated).
modelRef.features: Black sealed 2-way plug with locking tab on the alternator rear cover.

components.name: Alternator charge cable (B+)
components.description: Charge cable from the alternator B+ stud to the front power junction (and thus back to the battery through the main cable and master switch). Must pass through the master switch / isolator so the alternator is disconnected when the car is killed.
components.location: From alternator B+ along the engine/subframe to the front power junction near the passenger-side firewall.

factory.name: OE alternator positive cable in engine harness

raceOptions.name: 4 AWG fine-strand tinned copper in DR-25 or with heat sleeve, fused at junction (MIDI 175–200 A)
raceOptions.notes: Fuse protects the cable from a shorted alternator diode.

hardware.spec: Tinned copper, M8 hole, crimped with hydraulic hex crimper + adhesive heat shrink
Adel/EPDM-lined P-clamp, 13 mm ID, M6 screw

installNotes: Keep ≥ 150 mm from exhaust headers or use reflective heat sleeve.
inspection: Chafe points at engine-to-chassis transitions (engine moves on mounts).

modelRef.dimensions: 4 AWG fine-strand cable (Ø ~11 mm over jacket) with M8 ring lugs.
modelRef.features: Red jacket, tinned lugs with red heat-shrink boots.

components.name: Starter motor
components.description: Gear-reduction starter bolted to the engine block (Gen V LT starter uses the LS/LT-style 2-bolt mount). The solenoid S terminal is triggered by the ECM/PDM start output via a relay. Hot-restart ability is a common race problem: wrap the starter and its cable if headers are close.
components.location: Passenger side of the block at the bellhousing, low (below the exhaust manifold/header).

factory.name: GM Gen V LT gear-reduction starter
factory.notes: Part number not verified for 2016+ Camaro (forum listings vary); confirm with GM VIN lookup.

raceOptions.name: Lightweight high-torque mini starter for LS/LT
raceOptions.notes: Saves ~3–4 kg; choose a version clearing your headers and dry-sump pump. Check flywheel tooth count (168 vs 153) compatibility.

hardware.tool: 13 mm / 15 mm socket with long extension
hardware.notes: Bolt size/part from Michigan Motorsports listing; torque is the widely published GM LS/LT starter bolt value – confirm in GM SI.
Typical GM starter battery-terminal nut value.

hardware.spec: Reflective starter blanket (DEI/Thermo-Tec) secured with stainless ties

installNotes: Install after the engine/transmission is in the car (phase 6) but before headers if access is tight.
Check pinion-to-ring-gear engagement/clearance per the starter maker.
Connect the main positive cable and the S-terminal trigger; boot both.
inspection: Listen for slow/hot cranking (voltage drop on cables).

sources.title: ICT Billet Gen V LT starter bolt kit

images.title: Chevrolet Performance Gen V LT starter (Billy's Speed Shop)

modelRef.dimensions: Overall ~240 mm long, motor can Ø~85 mm, solenoid Ø~45 mm on top; 2 x M10 x 1.5 x 120 mm mounting bolts (GM 11610633).
modelRef.features: Black motor can, cast gear-reduction housing and 2-bolt flange to the passenger-side block rear, zinc solenoid on top with M8 battery stud and S-terminal, pinion nose into the bellhousing.

components.name: Starter trigger relay / PDM start channel
components.description: Start button → ECU/PDM logic → starter solenoid S terminal. With a PDM, use a high-current (20 A) channel with inhibit logic (clutch switch or neutral, engine not running, master ON). The OE starter solenoid draws high inrush; a dedicated 40 A relay close to the starter is also acceptable.
components.location: PDM channel in cabin, or relay on firewall near the starter wire exit.

factory.name: ECM-controlled starter relay (KR27) in underhood fuse block
factory.notes: Relay designation from typical GM convention; not verified for Gen 6.

installNotes: Include a clutch-pedal-down inhibit to avoid lurching in the pits.
inspection: Starter disengages immediately on button release.

modelRef.dimensions: Mini ISO relay 28 x 28 x 30 mm.
modelRef.features: Black cube relay with mounting tab and label.

components.name: Main battery positive cable (trunk to engine bay)
components.description: The long heavy cable from the battery (trunk, right side) through the master switch to the front power junction and starter. On a race car it runs inside the cabin along the passenger rocker/sill (inside the cage) and passes through the firewall with a sealed bulkhead stud or grommet. Size for the starter's cranking current with < 0.5 V total drop.
components.location: Trunk right → under/behind rear seat area → passenger-side sill inside cabin → passenger footwell → firewall bulkhead → starter.

factory.name: GM battery positive cable (aluminum/copper) run under the car
factory.notes: OE routes the positive cable along the underbody; a race car moves it inside the shell for protection.

raceOptions.name: 1/0 AWG fine-strand copper welding cable (EPDM jacket)
raceOptions.notes: ~5 m run; 1/0 gives low drop for a 6.2 L. 2 AWG acceptable with a light gear-reduction starter.

raceOptions.name: Aluminum battery cable (e.g. 0 AWG aluminum) for weight
raceOptions.notes: Requires tin-plated aluminum-rated lugs and anti-oxidant; larger gauge than copper for equal resistance.

hardware.spec: Tinned copper closed-end lugs 1/0, 3/8 in or M8 hole; hydraulic hex crimp; adhesive-lined heat shrink
EPDM-lined P-clamp, 16 mm ID, M6 rivnut + M6 screw every 300 mm
Rubber grommet sized to cable, sealed with RTV, or bulkhead power stud
Split nylon or Roundit sleeve over full length

installNotes: Plan this route during cage design (phase 1) so the cable passes inside cage tubes and away from seat/belt mounts.
Install rivnuts for P-clamps before paint.
Pull the cable before installing interior panels/seat; crimp lugs after final length is confirmed.
Measure voltage drop battery-to-starter while cranking (target < 0.5 V).
inspection: Look for chafing at every bulkhead and cage crossing.

sources.title: SCCA master switch rule discussion (switch in battery cable)

modelRef.dimensions: 1/0 AWG welding cable Ø ~15 mm, ≈5.2 m, 3/8" and M8 ring lugs.
modelRef.features: Red EPDM jacket, tinned copper lugs with red heat-shrink, runs battery + → ANL fuse → right sill → firewall → starter solenoid.

components.name: Front power junction / firewall bulkhead power stud
components.description: Insulated through-firewall power stud or junction block where the main cable, starter cable, alternator charge cable and the PDM feed meet. Also serves as the underhood remote jump point (the Gen 6 has an OE remote positive terminal for the same reason).
components.location: Passenger-side firewall, upper engine-bay side (x≈0.62, y≈0.70, z≈-0.35).

factory.name: Gen 6 underhood remote positive jump terminal / X50A fuse block feed

raceOptions.name: Blue Sea Systems PowerBar / insulated bulkhead stud
raceOptions.notes: 3/8 in stud, ≥ 250 A, with insulating cover.

installNotes: Seal the firewall pass-through (firewall must remain fire-tight per rules).

modelRef.dimensions: Insulated 2-stud power junction ~80 x 60 x 40 mm (estimated).
modelRef.features: Black insulated base, copper link bar, two 3/8" studs, red flip cover.

components.name: Starter cable (junction to starter)
components.description: Short heavy cable from the front power junction down to the starter solenoid B+ stud, in heat-reflective sleeve where it passes the headers.
components.location: Passenger-side firewall down to the starter.

raceOptions.name: 1/0 AWG copper with DEI Fire Sleeve

hardware.spec: Stainless clamps or silicone tape at ends

installNotes: Allow slack for engine movement on its mounts.

modelRef.dimensions: 1/0 AWG cable with DEI Fire Sleeve, M8 lug at the solenoid stud.
modelRef.features: Red jacket (or fire sleeve), tinned ring lugs with red boots.
